I have 16.9 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the full 16.9 mu for winter wheat and then the same 16.9 mu again for summer maize. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on water to keep yields stable, especially for wheat at overwintering, jointing, and grain filling, and for maize around the key growth stages. I have been farming a long time, so I will not chase fancy changes. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put on enough nitrogen first, add phosphorus for rooting, and some potassium to keep the crop steady. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives me a reliable harvest on this rotation. Because I am 70, I will keep field work simple and timely: rotary tillage for wheat after maize, and no-tillage for maize after wheat to save time and catch the sowing window. I will spray only as much as needed to control common weeds, aphids, rust, armyworm, and other usual problems. My goal is stable production, not taking big risks, and not making the work heavier than necessary.
